Check before applying it: Name the unit of the decision (identity, occurrence or resource) and count incorrect and split pairs in that unit
Observed in this study: SCA: the alias key joined 43 pairs of different occurrences, and the occurrence key split 43 pairs of the same identity. Terraform: a file-and-property key joined four resources (54 incorrect pairs)

Check before applying it: Measure retention in occurrence units, not only in visible identities
Observed in this study: SCA: one alert per identity kept 2 of 6 supported occurrences while both identities stayed visible

Check before applying it: Apply a PASS result or a suppression at the scope of the property, not of the file
Observed in this study: A file-level PASS removed all four Terraform resources and 6 of 8 Kubernetes containers; on Terraform, a resource-level PASS removed none (counterfactual)

Check before applying it: Compute what the stage alone supports (Equation (4)) in the unit of the decision, regardless of its time or output volume
Observed in this study: Without the image scan or the source SCA stage, 3 of 6 occurrences were lost while both identities stayed visible. The slowest profiles supported nothing unique, and a 2.1 s profile was the only source of four properties

Check before applying it: Check which artifact types the mode analyzes
Observed in this study: Trivy in filesystem mode reported nothing on JAR archives that its rootfs mode analyzed

Check before applying it: Test overrides of Pod-level settings, multi-container workloads and every container type
Observed in this study: Trivy passed containers that override a Pod-level runAsNonRoot, and no tool flagged an ephemeral container

Check before applying it: Check job-level permissions before acting on a file-level alert
Observed in this study: Checkov flagged w03 and w06, whose jobs could not write, and not w04 and w05, whose jobs could

Check before applying it: Check that the report exists and has content, not only that the step succeeded
Observed in this study: A run concluded successfully although its authenticated DAST pass produced no alerts and was recorded as failed

Check before applying it: Pin and record the image digests and the vulnerability database snapshot
Observed in this study: 330 advisory identifiers appeared and 4 disappeared on one image tag between two runs about 30 h apart, with the same tool versions

Check before applying it: Check the findings that carry no CWE
Count true findings lost next to false alerts removed, keep the alert on abstention or invalid output, and review every dismissal against the evidence it cites
Observed in this study: Q-C removed none of the 11 false alerts and four supported items, and each dismissal cited real evidence that it misread
